hospital_task.vehicle_note: 与普通车辆使用完全相同的车辆性能、道路权限和安全跟驰参数

assumptions: Six fixed OD demands are independent of the number of route candidates; each OD requests one vehicle every 30 seconds before 1200 seconds.
The 600-1200 second speed restriction is an assumed engineering event, not an observed accident, measured capacity reduction or reconstructed real traffic window.

Only west-to-hospital departures at or after event publication and during its active interval may reconsider their route. Compare the complete same-endpoint candidates, including the default, using sum(external segment length/current known speed); ties retain the default.
Route-cost estimates use the current known restriction without anticipating its future end; they omit uncalibrated junction/queue delays and are not actual trip-time observations.
Both the primary 1 m/s event and the predeclared 0.5 m/s severity sensitivity are reported in full, including unchanged policies or worse outcomes.
All routes are assigned before scheduled departure; vehicles already assigned are not rerouted in the network. Future hospital tasks do not affect earlier decisions.
Hospital tasks share the same assumed_car type as background traffic; there is no special speed, signal priority, lane privilege or traffic-rule exemption.
S3 here tests the task interface and independent route guidance only; coordinated governance B is not implemented.
All findings are engineering diagnostics under assumptions, not validated real-world governance effects. A longer detour may worsen results.
